The Julius/Sir James contrast, the Vandemeyer warning and the 'businesslike' marriage exchange all survive adequately.

strengths: All six verbatim passages survive exactly, including the italicised Vandemeyer warning and the closing taunt.
The 24th / 'any need to hurry' exchange and Julius cutting off the lawyer are retained, preserving the planned suspicion of Julius.
Tommy's 'too damned businesslike' outburst stays paired with the cold rebuke and the 'I feel heated' reply.
The begging-terrier sequence keeps the 'British phlegm' comic beat.
summary: The revision keeps the plot spine, all six verbatim lines, the continuity checks (24th, two o'clock meeting, Julius finds the packet, Tommy's ink idea) and the misleading photo puzzlement. However, its extra trimming beyond the first draft creates attribution and connective defects. The Little Willie speech no longer has a speaker and follows Sir James's lines directly. 'On the other hand' and 'Nevertheless' have lost their antecedents, and Sir James's maxim no longer answers Julius's complacency. Smaller losses affect turn-taking on the train and the false-triumph beat before the taunt.
